The snakeboard is assumed to follow the kinematics given by Equation 5. The feedback controller presented in this section is similar to the previously conceived controller,¹⁴ which minimizes a position error function by specifying a desired angular velocity, θ̇_d, of the snakeboard body. The driving velocity, v, is assumed to be given, as it is achieved by the dynamic controller. Equation 4 relates θ̇ to the steering angle, φ. Given the output, θ̇_d, from the feedback controller and the current velocity, the desired steering angle is
φ_d = tan⁻¹ (lθ̇_d / v) . (25)
If the control is chosen to be u_k = τ_φ, then the desired steering angle in Equation 25 can be achieved by a PID control,
τ_φ = k_p ε_φ + k_d ε̇_φ + ∫₀ᵗ ε_φ dt . (26)
where ε_φ = φ_d − φ, and the gains, k_p, k_d and k_i, are tuned accordingly.
III.1.1. Reference Configurations

The reference configuration is denoted by q_r = (x_r, y_r, θ_r)ᵀ, and is located on a reference path, R(s) = (x_R(s), y_R(s), θ_R(s))ᵀ, parameterized by a path parameter, s. If the snakeboard has a current configuration, q_c = (x_c, y_c, θ_c)ᵀ, then the reference configuration is the point, R(s_min), where
s_min = arg min_{s∈(0,∞)} ‖q_c − R(s)‖ , (27)
where the norm, ‖q_c − R(s)‖, is defined by
‖q_c − R(s)‖ = √((x_c − x_R(s))² + (y_c − y_R(s))² + d²(θ_c − θ_R(s))²) ,
Here, d² is the radius of gyration of the snakeboard. Therefore, q_r is the point on R(s) such that the distance between q_r and q_c is a minimum.
III.1.2. The Error Configuration
The error function that is to be minimized by the kinematic controller, q_e, is defined as the error configuration. It is found by the transformation,
q_e = (x_e ; y_e ; θ_e) = [cos θ_c sin θ_c 0 ; −sin θ_c cos θ_c 0 ; 0 0 1] (q_r − q_c) . (28)
As can be seen in Equation 28, if q_c = q_r, then q_e = 0. Figure 3 shows the geometric interpretation of this configuration transformation.

This section describes the controller selected for path tracking and shows that it is locally stable around the error configuration, q_e = (0, 0, 0)ᵀ. In order for the error configuration to converge to zero, q̇_e should drive the error to zero. From Equation 28,
